one_line: Name the parent's exact problem in the first line over the product already in use, then cut every two seconds.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 medium shot: a toddler's head over a BLISS cardboard box. Subtitles, in step with the voice: "אם גם הילד", "לא מפסיק לטפס", "על הרהיטים בבית", "זה בדיוק בשבילך". 0:02 cut to round foam pods in a row.
q1_hook.why: A problem every parent of a climber knows opens the first sentence and addresses "your child" (H1, K6), spoken and subtitled together (H6). The box hints at a reveal and the pods are in use by 1.7 s (S1, H2). The narrator has no face (H4 partly).

beats.what: A toddler's head over a BLISS box, then he runs past; "אם גם הילד", "לא מפסיק לטפס"
beats.why: The problem, with a box hinting at a reveal

beats.what: Cut to a row of round pods on the carpet; he steps onto the first; "זה בדיוק בשבילך"
beats.why: The solution appears in 2 s, no wait

beats.what: Tight shots: he lifts a pod; "תכירו את הסטפס של"; his name is said at 0:07 (transcript)
beats.why: Names the product and gives the personal angle

beats.what: He lifts and stacks pods into a tower; "מטפס", "קופץ", "משחק חדש"
beats.why: Shows the building game the voice names

beats.what: He steps and jumps along the row; "להשתחרר ופשוט לעוף עם"
Overhead tight shots of him lifting, pushing and stepping on pods; "בליס מלווים"
beats.why: Variety of angle while the voice lists stages

beats.what: He moves pods around on the carpet; "משתלב בבית מושלם", "אקססורי"
beats.why: Adds a second need: it looks good at home

beats.what: He steps on pods; "תיכנסי לבליס"; ends on the empty row with a BLISS overlay
beats.why: A single ask after the benefits

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: None. The caption names the product and a feeling about the child's excitement; no question, tag, save or send ask.
q2_flow.why: The problem line is answered by the pods from 1.7 s, so there is no wait (H2). A view every 2 s keeps things moving (R3). But picture and voice drift ("jumps" is said at 0:09, shown at 0:16) and 0:18 to 0:33 repeats the same toddler-and-pods action with no new idea (R3, R1).

q3_cta.what: Spoken (transcript) and subtitled at 0:33 to 0:38: "אז אם גם את מחפשת", "תיכנסי לבליס", "ותמצאי בדיוק את מה". Caption: no ask, only "הסטפס של Bliss" and a feeling line.
q3_cta.why: Said and shown last, after the benefits, one action only (C1, C6). But it sends viewers to the whole brand with no link or comment word, and the subtitle sits in the bottom 35% (C6, C3 not used).

q4_shown.what: A toddler with round foam stepping pods in a living room: stepping along a row (0:03), lifting (0:05), stacking a tower (0:12), jumping off (0:17), pushing pods around (0:28). BLISS on a box (0:00) and as an overlay (0:02, 0:37). No price or sizes.
q4_shown.why: The pods are in use from 1.7 s, and the claims, climb, stack, jump, mostly have a shot (S1, K5). A mother speaks first-hand about years with the brand (S6). The child's face and name appear together (said at 0:07, written in the caption), which S5 warns against.

q5_edit.what: About 20 views in 38 s, about 1.9 s each, straight cuts, no speed change seen. Subtitles of one to four words follow the voiceover. BLISS overlay at 0:02 to 0:03 and at 0:37. Ends on the empty row of pods.
q5_edit.why: A new view every 1 to 3 s with short subtitles keeps the pace brisk (E2, E4), and tight overhead shots add variety (R3). It ends right after the last line (E8), but 38 s of script is long for one idea (R2).

q6_topic.what: A mother says her toddler cannot stop climbing furniture and that foam stepping pods give him a safe outlet that suits the home. Serves parents of climbing toddlers.
q6_topic.why: A real toddler problem named in the first line, so the right parent self-selects (K6, H1). "Looks good in the home" adds a second need, design (K6). The mood is calm, with no gift, occasion or high peak (K1, K7 not met).

q7_filmed.what: Phone footage in a tidy beige living room, soft daylight: static wide shots of the row of pods, handheld overhead and tight shots of the toddler. Eye level for the hook. The narrator is never seen. A toddler alone on camera.
q7_filmed.why: Clean frames with the pods large read well at phone size (F4, F7). The home setting is native (H8), but the tidy neutral room and the BLISS overlay lean toward an ad look (H8, H3). Subtitles at about 75% height sit in the bottom 35% (F2).

q8_text.on_screen: Small white sans subtitles, no box, at about 75% of the frame height, one to four words at a time, in step with the voice: "אם גם הילד" (0:00), "לא מפסיק לטפס" (0:01), "על הרהיטים בבית" (0:02), "זה בדיוק בשבילך" (0:03), "מטפס" (0:08), "קופץ" (0:09), "תיכנסי לבליס" (0:36). BLISS overlay top-centre at 0:02 and 0:37. The child's name is subtitled at 0:07.
q8_text.caption: "הסטפס של Bliss". Two short lines: the product name, then a feeling line about the child's excitement with the child's name and an emoji. No hashtags, question, CTA or disclosure words.
q8_text.why: Short synced subtitles carry the problem line from 0:00, so it works muted (T1, T3). The thin white text at about 75% height sits in the bottom 35% over cream and beige (T4, T5). The caption names the product but has no problem keywords, no hashtags and no disclosure words (T7, T8).

weak_points: Scripted, generic voiceover; subtitles in the bottom 35%; the CTA sends to a whole brand with no link; no price or sizes; picture and voice drift; the child's face and name together; no disclosure words.
lumebook_takeaway: Open with the parent's problem line as subtitles over the product already in use, cut every 2 s, and end on one CTA. Hands only, no child.
not_verified: Music (cannot hear; the transcript holds only the voiceover). Whether the child is the narrator's son (the caption names him). The pods' product name and price. The first pass counts about 24 shots; I count about 20 distinct views. Whether the BLISS wording on the wall is an added overlay (it looks like one). Paid-partnership label: media info says 0; bliss.il is a coauthor.
